abstract: BACKGROUND: Testicular germ cell tumour (TGCT) is the most common cancer in young men, and an imbalance between the estrogen and androgen levels in utero is hypothesized to influence TGCT risk. Thus, polymorphisms in genes involved in the action of sex hormones may contribute to variability in an individual's susceptibility to TGCT. METHODS: We conducted a Norwegian-Swedish case-parent study. A total of 105 single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in 20 sex hormone pathway genes were genotyped using Sequenom MassArray iPLEX Gold, in 831 complete triads and 474 dyads. To increase the statistical power, the analysis was expanded to include 712 case singletons and 3922 Swedish controls, thus including triads, dyads and the case-control samples in a single test for association. Analysis for allelic associations was performed with the UNPHASED program, using a likelihood-based association test for nuclear families with missing data, and odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated. False discovery rate (FDR) was used to adjust for multiple testing. RESULTS: Five genetic variants across the ESR2 gene [encoding estrogen receptor beta (ERβ)] were statistically significantly associated with the risk of TGCT. In the case-parent analysis, the markers rs12434245 and rs10137185 were associated with a reduced risk of TGCT (OR = 0.66 and 0.72, respectively; both FDRs <5%), whereas rs2978381 and rs12435857 were associated with an increased risk of TGCT (OR = 1.21 and 1.19, respectively; both FDRs <5%). In the combined case-parent/case-control analysis, rs12435857 and rs10146204 were associated with an increased risk of TGCT (OR = 1.15 and 1.13, respectively; both FDRs <5%), whereas rs10137185 was associated with a reduced risk of TGCT (OR = 0.79, FDR <5%). In addition, we found that three genetic variants in CYP19A1 (encoding aromatase) were statistically significantly associated with the risk of TGCT in the case-parent analysis. The T alleles of the rs2414099, rs8025374 and rs3751592 SNPs were associated with an increased risk of TGCT (OR = 1.30, 1.30 and 1.21, respectively; all FDRs <5%). We found no statistically significant differences in allelic effect estimates between parental inherited genetic variation in the sex hormone pathways and TGCT risk in the offspring, and no evidence of heterogeneity between seminomas and non-seminomas, or between the Norwegian and the Swedish population, in any of the SNPs examined. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings provide support for ERβ and aromatase being implicated in the aetiology of TGCT. Exploring the functional role of the TGCT risk-associated SNPs will further elucidate the biological mechanisms involved.
abstract_ja: 背景：精巣胚細胞腫瘍(TGCT)は若年男性に最も多い悪性腫瘍であり、子宮内でのエストロゲンとアンドロゲンのバランスの不均衡がTGCTのリスクに影響すると考えられている。そこで、性ホルモンの作用に関与する遺伝子の多型が、TGCTへの感受性の個人差に寄与している可能性がある。方法：ノルウェー・スウェーデンの家族・症例対照研究を実施した。性ホルモン経路の20遺伝子にある105の一塩基多型(SNP)をSequenom MassArray iPLEX Goldで遺伝子型解析し、完全な家系(トリオ)831組、ディアド474組を対象とした。統計検定力を高めるため、解析にはさらに症例単独712例とスウェーデン人対照3922例を加え、トリオ、ディアド、症例対照データを一つの検定にまとめて関連解析を行った。対立遺伝子関連解析はUNPHASEDプログラムを用い、欠測データを伴う核家族に対する尤度ベースの関連検定を行い、オッズ比(OR)と95%信頼区間(CI)を算出した。多重比較の補正には偽発見率(FDR)を用いた。結果：ESR2遺伝子(エストロゲン受容体β(ERβ)をコードする)内の5つの遺伝子変異がTGCTのリスクと統計学的に有意に関連した。家系解析では、マーカーrs12434245とrs10137185はTGCTリスクの低下と関連した(OR = 0.66および0.72、いずれもFDR <5%)。一方、rs2978381とrs12435857はリスク増加と関連した(OR = 1.21および1.19、いずれもFDR <5%)。症例家系・症例対照の統合解析では、rs12435857とrs10146204がリスク増加と関連し(OR = 1.15および1.13、いずれもFDR <5%)、rs10137185はリスク低下と関連した(OR = 0.79、FDR <5%)。さらに、CYP19A1(アロマターゼをコードする)内の3つの遺伝子変異が、家系解析においてTGCTリスクと統計学的に有意に関連した。rs2414099、rs8025374、rs3751592のT対立遺伝子はリスク増加と関連した(OR = 1.30、1.30、1.21、いずれもFDR <5%)。親から遺伝した性ホルモン経路の遺伝的変異と子のTGCTリスクとの間の対立遺伝子効果の推定値には統計学的有意差は認められず、検討したいずれのSNPでもセミノーマと非セミノーマの間、またノルウェー人集団とスウェーデン人集団の間に不均一性の証拠は認められなかった。結論：本研究の結果は、ERβとアロマターゼがTGCTの病因に関与することを支持する。TGCTリスクに関連するSNPの機能的役割を検討することで、関与する生物学的機序がさらに明らかになるであろう。
